articles.title: ‘I’m Shocked That People Are Still Playing’ – How GTA 5 Took Over the World
articles.summary: Could GTA 6 be as big as its predecessor? We take a look at how GTA 5 became one of the biggest games in history, selling over 230m copies and being played by millions of people every week for over a decade.
body: There are over 230 million copies of Grand Theft Auto 5 in the world. As the second-highest selling game of all time, it has been played for billions of hours by players across the globe, making it one of the most significant pastimes in the entire world. That’s an impressive achievement for what in 2013 was simply the highly-anticipated next entry in Rockstar’s beloved (and notorious) open-world crime series. But GTA 5 proved to be much, much more than a typical sequel. It has become home to a huge, expressive, and loyal community, one which has made a digital hobby of everything from warring alien clans to producing slick vehicle stunt movies.
This is the story of how a video game became much more than a crime simulator.
points: We take a look at how GTA 5 became one of the biggest games in history, selling over 230m copies and being played by millions of people every week for over a decade.

articles.title: To Reinvent a Stephen King Classic, Mike Flanagan Needed "One of the Best Actors I’ve Ever Met"
articles.summary: But in Flanagan's latest, a modern reimagining of the Stephen King classic, Carrie, Sloyan rolls those various elements up into perhaps her greatest role yet: Margaret White (aka Carrie's mom).
body: Samantha Sloyan has played various roles across the Mike Flanagan horror universe, both empathetic and extremely hateable. Her scheming, self-righteous Bev Keane was the standout performance of Midnight Mass. In Midnight Club, she played a witchy herbalist with a dark secret. And she was a calming presence as Leigh Crain in his breakout Netflix hit, The Haunting of Hill House.

Sloyan's version of Margaret is far more complex and nuanced than the one depicted by Piper Laurie in Brian De Palma's 1976 film, or even the version in King's original novella. Flanagan tears the story of Carrie down to its studs and builds something new, with Margaret playing a more important role than ever before, though she's still a tragic figure, at best.
"I think she fails her daughter in a lot of ways," Sloyan tells Polygon. "She's loving her in the wrong way."

Polygon connected with Samantha Sloyan over Zoom to discuss playing Maragret White in Carrie, how she approaches playing complex villains, and what it's like being part of Mike Flanagan's troupe of recurring actors. Flanagan himself also weighed in to praise Sloyan.
points: But in Flanagan's latest, a modern reimagining of the Stephen King classic, Carrie, Sloyan rolls those various elements up into perhaps her greatest role yet: Margaret White (aka Carrie's mom).

articles.title: Wildwood Review
articles.summary: Review: Wildwood is an arresting, exciting fantasy epic made all the more impressive by the fact that it’s handmade and hand-animated, even if some story stumbles occasionally hold it back.
body: There’s something wondrous about the transportive power of stop-motion animated films when they’re executed at the standard that Laika sets for themselves, and wonder is certainly the name of the game in Wildwood. Adapted from the first novel in Colin Meloy and Carson Ellis’ Wildwood Chronicles, Wildwood sees director Travis Knight and the craftspeople at Laika turning in a staggeringly beautiful and surprisingly dark fantasy adventure that boasts exciting action, enchanting and enchanted natural settings, and talking woodland creatures with jobs… and that’s all before the characters leave Portland to journey into Wildwood!

Long stretches of the film achieve such a sense of immersion that, at its most effective, it’s easy to forget that Wildwood is a stop-motion film at all, a sensation that’s even more impressive when taking into account the wide array of fantasy trappings that Wildwood deploys.
points: Review: Wildwood is an arresting, exciting fantasy epic made all the more impressive by the fact that it’s handmade and hand-animated, even if some story stumbles occasionally hold it back.

articles.title: Godzilla Minus Zero Trailer Reveals Sneak Peek at King Ghidorah's Gravity Beams
articles.summary: Toho's latest Godzilla Minus Zero trailer is here and puts the spotlight on King Ghidorah's lightning-like gravity beams and Godzilla's iconic atomic breath.
body: This new sneak peek at the King of the Monsters and the latest iteration of his archnemesis debuted as part of New York Comic Con 2026. Toho refrained from showing its new design for Ghidorah yet again, but there's still plenty of new footage to see in the one-minute video.

How did Noriko Oishi (Minami Hamabe) survive Godzilla's first attack? That's the question Godzilla Minus Zero teases an answer for in its second full-length trailer. It looks like viewers are in for pure carnage this time around, as the three-headed kaiju zaps any airborne structures out of the sky left and right. You can see how the sequel's returning human crew will "fight fire with fire" next month in the trailer below.

With less than a month until its premiere, it seems the filmmakers behind the Godzilla Minus One sequel are going to save the full Ghidorah reveal for those who go to the theater. We'll at least know how the character has been redesigned for the Minus universe when it premieres November 6.

body: The trailer begins with a doctor suggesting that Noriko had "no business surviving" the events of Godzilla Minus One before cutting to Koichi flying through a supernatural storm, lifting entire houses far up into the air. Cue a sizzle reel of people running from or discussing how they're scared of the impending threat, all culminating with a massive atomic breath attack from Godzilla.

That said, Godzilla doesn't seem to be the only monster humans will face in this movie. The trailer's description alludes to "a new threat," and while it doesn't show another creature, it hints at one. Namely, while Godzilla's attacks have a blue hue in Godzilla Minus One and this trailer, we also see beams attacking civilians and destroying a bomb at certain points in the trailer that look more yellow or lightning-like.

articles.title: Halo Already Delivered the Perfect Master Chief Origin Story, 25 Years Ago
articles.summary: Late last month, Xbox announced that development of the next game set in the Halo universe would be handed off to Activision. Then, earlier this week, a leak shared by Rebs Gaming indicated that Activision is considering a hard reboot that would double as Master Chief’s origin story.
body: Like many gamers in the early 2000s, I got an Xbox specifically so I could play Halo: Combat Evolved. I became so obsessed with it that I bought everything I could find with “Halo” on the cover, including Eric Nylund’s Halo: The Fall of Reach. I didn’t expect it to completely change how I looked at Master Chief, but it did, chronicling his experience as a child abducted into an experimental military program designed to create supersoldiers. The armored, weathered combat veteran from the game, like the rest of us, was once a kid. But even at only six years old, he was special.

The Fall of Reach begins decades before Combat Evolved, in the year 2517, when Dr. Catherine Halsey identifies John as one of 150 children genetically suited for the SPARTAN-II program. These children are abducted and replaced with short-lived flash clones designed to trick their parents into thinking each child is dead. He's then subjected to years of military training under Chief Petty Officer Franklin Mendez. All of this occurs on the planet Reach which, aside from Earth, is positioned as the next most-prominent human world.

Then, earlier this week, a leak shared by Rebs Gaming indicated that Activision is considering a hard reboot that would double as Master Chief’s origin story.

articles.title: Escape from EloHello has me reliving my worst online PvP nightmares in roguelike-form
articles.summary: I was stuck in elo hell for a good four years, then I entered elo purgatory for another five years, and now I'm apparently in elo heaven, but for some reason it still feels like elo hell. I guess that's just part and parcel of playing online competitive multiplayer games.
body: While I'd never want to relive the pain of climbing from Bronze to GM, I am morbidly intrigued in whether I still have that fight in me. So I've found a happy medium, playing a strategy roguelike that provides players with "all the satisfaction of reaching rank 1, none of the toxic teammates or 40-minute hostage games".

In Escape from EloHell, you're set the task of collecting MMR as you climb the ladder from Iron 4 to Challenger, rank 1 in just 60 matches, before the season resets and you have to start again. The only way to gain MMR is to win matches, but unlike an ordinary competitive multiplayer, Escape from EloHell is a roguelike in which you have to gamble on your ability to win matches to gain effects which will help you in the long run.

articles.title: This Control-inspired action game set in a 'planet-scale alien mind' has one of the most stunning art styles I've seen this year
articles.summary: In the age of near photorealism, it takes a lot for a game's visuals to impress me. As cramming yet more pixels into a videogame character's face provides diminishing returns, standing out from the crowd is increasingly about how creative developers get in applying that power.
body: Created by LA-based developer Studio Lifeforms, Etre is a narrative driven-action game set on Orbis, which Studio Lifeforms describes as a "planet-scale alien mind on the brink of awakening". You play as a character named Xyle, who arrives at this sentient cityscape in search of his soulmate Atel.

According to Studio Lifeforms, the game's distinctive visuals are inspired by graphic novels of the '70s and '80s. Studio Lifeforms doesn't specify which graphics novels, and I am too much of a comics philistine to tell you. But the result is an incredibly distinctive visual style. In terms of games, Etre's closest visual cousins are the likes of Rez and Tetris Effect. But Etre applies its aesthetics to a much more grounded type of game.

From a mechanical perspective, Studio Lifeforms cites Remedy's Control as the primary influence, with the game letting you explore Orbis in a semi-open fashion, while the story will be shaped by your actions on Orbis. Like Control, Etre features a highly movement-based combat system. Also like Control, the enemies you fight are super weird, including environmental anomalies and "living geometry."
points: In the age of near photorealism, it takes a lot for a game's visuals to impress me.
As cramming yet more pixels into a videogame character's face provides diminishing returns, standing out from the crowd is increasingly about how creative developers get in applying that power.

articles.title: "We have to go a different path" - Krafton thinks PUBG Ded.Net's pulpy gameshow hyperviolence and roguelite twist can make it the next big battle royale
articles.summary: Player Unknown's Battlegrounds is arguably one of the most important games to release in the past decade. If H1Z1 built the foundation of the battle royale genre, PUBG certainly shaped it into the form that remains hugely successful today.
body: Fortnite might have stolen the battle royale crown, but PUBG's name still means something even today. So when publisher Krafton announced a brand-new PUBG was in the works last month, it was an immediately exciting prospect for battle royale fans. And doubtless a daunting one for its development team, given the large shoes Ded.Net has to fill.

But what does it mean to make a new PUBG in the shadow of the original? How do you make something familiar, while keeping it fresh enough that it doesn't feel redundant? The answer may lie in Ded.Net; a grungy splatterfest being developed by Krafton's Wisconsin studio, PUBG Madison, that gives those battle royale fundamentals a more rogue-like spin. To find out more, I spoke with creative director Dave Curd about the challenges and opportunities facing the team.

"I was charged with spreading the gospel of PUBG to an audience that might not already appreciate it or like it or understand it," Curd told me at Gamescom. And that required breaking it down to its fundamentals. "What is PUBG? Is it a blue Zone? Is it the level three helmet? I think [it's] desperate survival. I think it's survival of the fittest, it's dog eat dog."
points: Player Unknown's Battlegrounds is arguably one of the most important games to release in the past decade.
If H1Z1 built the foundation of the battle royale genre, PUBG certainly shaped it into the form that remains hugely successful today.

articles.title: 'I'm the type of player who loves to 100% a game': SungWon Cho on achievement hunting, why he doesn’t like multiplayer games, and the one Balatro joker that nearly drove him to despair
articles.summary: Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex.
body: Welcome to Disk Cleanup, our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?"

SungWon Cho got into PC gaming through the children's adventure games developed by Humongous Entertainment. "Games like Freddi Fish, Spy Fox, those really stuck with me," says the YouTuber and actor. "I remember playing those at a pretty young age and just being obsessed with the characters, the dialogue. I don't really play adventure games now, but I did then."

Cho stepped away from the mic to give me a guided tour of his Steam library, which he reserves specifically for games he wants to lock into: "If I know I'm going to be obsessed with a game, I like to play it on PC," he says. Truer words were never spoken.
On PC, I'm not playing anything currently. I think the last game I got really into on PC was Dave the Diver.
points: Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom.
He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex.

articles.title: Phasmophobia confirms 30 million sales as its Crimson Eye Halloween event returns
articles.summary: Phasmophobia has sold more than 30 million copies across PC and console since it launched in Early Access in 2020.
body: Developer Kinetic Games shared the milestone alongside confirming the return of Crimson Eye, its annual Halloween event, which is now live and runs until 1st November.

Crimson Eye brings blood moon weather to a rotating set of maps each day, which makes ghosts faster and drains your sanity more quickly, but pays out more in return. The event maps are Tanglewood Drive, Camp Woodwind, Grafton Farmhouse, Bleasdale Farmhouse, Point Hope (standard only), Edgefield Road, Nell's Diner, and Willow Street.
Community goals unlock the Beholder ID Card and Badge, and the Blood Moon Trophy, while personal goals unlock the Blood Moon Charm, a seasonal t-shirt, and upgrades to the Crimson Eye trophy.

If that's not quite enough for you, watch two hours' worth of Phasmophobia streams on Twitch between 8th and 15th October and you'll get a Crimson Eye t-shirt cosmetic. You can also earn double XP and rewards from 15th to 22nd October.

articles.title: Squadron 42 opens for Steam wishlisting ahead of a planned Q2 2027 release
articles.summary: Squadron 42, the single-player spin-off of Star Citizen, can now be wishlisted on Steam ahead of its planned Q2 2027 release.
body: Developer Cloud Imperium Games announced the news on 10th October alongside a new trailer, which you can see below.

The game is set in the year 2945, with the United Empire of Earth on the brink of collapse. You enlist as a rookie in the UEE Navy, stationed aboard a capital ship, where you'll live and work alongside a crew as you work your way up the ranks of a galactic war.
Cloud Imperium says it mixes space combat with ground operations, stealth sections, and "quieter moments" with the people around you, with decisions to make alongside your crewmates.

The cast is kind of staggering. It includes Mark Hamill, Gary Oldman, Gillian Anderson, Ben Mendelsohn, Henry Cavill, Andy Serkis, John Rhys-Davies, Jonathan Bailey, Mark Strong, Alix Wilton Regan, Damson Idris, Liam Cunningham, and Jane Perry, among others, all captured through full performance capture.

videos.title: The Witcher 3 Remastered: PC Performance Review + Optimised Settings
videos.summary: Thanks to Alienware for sponsoring our PC performance reviews. To learn more about the Alienware AREA-51 Gaming Desktop, check out:
body: Note on texture quality/VRAM: The on-screen VRAM figures are from RTX 5090 testing at 4K DLAA with RT disabled. The recommendation of High textures for 8GB GPUs is based on separate RTX 4060 testing, also with RT disabled, where VRAM usage remained below 7GB.

Having already delivered the Complete Edition, CD Projekt RED still has plans for The Witcher 3, hence the arrival of the controversial Remastered release - and while it has some key improvements, there are still some issues. In our PC performance review, we present the top-line changes to the game then compare the hotfix 5.00C version to the latest patch 5.01 before we dive head-first into those all-important optimised settings.

videos.title: Nintendo Switch Sports Resort – Overview Trailer – Nintendo Switch 2
videos.summary: The Nintendo Switch Sports Resort game launches October 22, 2026, exclusively on the Nintendo Switch 2 system. Pre-orders are available now:
body: The latest game in the intuitive sports series is coming to Nintendo Switch 2!
Get moving solo or with family and friends across 12 immersive sports. Aim for the target’s center in Archery, knock down pins in Bowling, duke it out in Boxing, and more!
You can also explore the island! Use Joy-Con 2 mouse controls in Skateboarding, steer across the waves in Power Cruising, and tilt the controller to fly around freely in Prop Plane.
